Sachin: Quick heads-up — nightly TP job shows a sharp perf cliff for all-reduce around certain message sizes. Profiling suggests packetization/padding creates small-frag bursts that force NCCL into a suboptimal path (tree fallback + small-kernel). Raw numbers below.

Sachin: ```
run: nightly/tp8/modelX
tp: 8, microbatch: 4, seq: 1024
observed message sizes (bytes): [48k, 60k, 64k, 68k, 128k]
p50/p95/p99 all-reduce latency (ms): 1.8 / 12.4 / 34.9  <-- big tail at those mid sizes
throughput tokens/s: -9% vs baseline
trace excerpt:
  comm_send(64k) -> split into 3 frags: 24k/24k/16k -> handshake overhead + kernel switch
  nccl_op: ring start -> fallback_tree at chunk 2
```

Yuki: Do you have a repro script? Is KV cache warmup interacting (prefix caching produces variable packetization)?

Sachin: Repro steps (quick):
1) checkout branch `tp-repro/packetize-24k`
2) run `./bench_tp.py --gpus 8 --mb 4 --seq 1024 --profile`
3) input is long prompts (varied prompt lengths) which creates uneven tensor slices

I tried with KV cache cold vs warm: warm makes it worse because cached prefixes change the per-GPU send size distribution. KV coalescing was not stable across steps (see logs).

Tess: Can you try forcing NCCL to ring-only vs tree-only to confirm? Also, what does kernel selector select for those fragment sizes? Might be falling back to a slow small-frag path.

Sachin: Tried env toggles:
```
# force ring
export NCCL_ALGO=ring
# force tree
export NCCL_ALGO=tree
```
Results: ring-only still had tail for 64k bursts (latency improved slightly), tree-only reduced p99 but reduced avg throughput (higher CPU); interestingly kernel selector logs show `kernel_path=small_frag` for <32k chunks and `kernel_path=vectorized` otherwise. Fragmentation produced many <32k chunks.

Maria: This smells like two interacting heuristics: (1) NCCL rendezvous chunking threshold, (2) our kernel autoswitch threshold. If chunks land on the wrong side of the boundary we lose comm/compute overlap and see handshakes.

David: Proposal: make the kernel selector padding-aware + introduce a coalescing step that pads to the preferred kernel boundary (e.g., 32k or 64k) instead of leaving uneven fragments. Also add metric: `allreduce.frag_size_histogram` and a `kernel_path` tag.

Sachin: Agree. I have a tiny experiment: align chunk sizes to 256B and prefer packing so min_frag >= 32k. Microbenchmark:
```
before: p99=34.9ms
after (align 256B + min_frag 32k): p99=18.7ms, throughput +6%
```
But corner cases: increased padding may raise bytes sent (cost) in some configs, and some NCCL topologies prefer smaller chunks.

perf-bot: ci/perf: tp-allreduce-packetize (id: 2026-03-17-88) shows regression on one test: +12% p99 on small batches, baseline improved on mid-sized batches. Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/2026/2026-03-17-88

Tess: :eyes: Can we open a tracking ticket and a canary patch? We need to avoid global perf regressions.

Sachin: Will open ticket and a small PR for kernel selector change + opt-in flag `RDW_KVPACK_PAD_MODE=adaptive` so we can canary. Assigning to @Yuki for validation and @Tess for rollout plan.

Yuki: I'll validate on 4 hardware shapes (A100x8, H100x8, V100x8, dedicated on-prem cluster). I want histograms from perf collector and a per-route fallback metric. Will try edge cases: very small microbatches + long sequence.

David: Also add a fallback policy: if padding increases bytes_sent by >8% rollback kernel change automatically for that route.

Sachin: Good call. I'll push the PR with conservative defaults and add the metrics. Will post results in this thread when CI finishes. Thanks :thumbsup:

perf-bot: ci/perf: baseline vs pr#4521 — microbench results uploaded to dashboard.

Sachin: (follow-up) CI artifacts show the p99 improvements on our nightly but one customer sim shows +3% byte-cost. I'll attach a small knob to disable padding per-route.

Tess: Nice. Keep the PR small, include unit tests for chunker and an integration test that asserts no >10% regression on bytes_sent for any route.

Sachin: Will do. Next update in ~2 hours with CI run.
